editorial_contributions.text:
The author studies the properties of Fano surfaces with a fixed number of elliptic curves. We recall that a Fano surface is a surface of general type parametrizing the lines of a smooth cubic threefold.

The paper gives an application of the results of a previous work [Manuscr. Math. 129, No. 3, 381--399 (2009; Zbl 1177.14079)], to the case of surfaces having 12 or 30 elliptic curves, describing the first ones as ramified triple covers of an abelian surface and computing their Néron-Severi group. In the latter case, the author focuses on the Fermat cubic, explicitly computing the configuration of the 30 elliptic curves and the generators of the Néron-Severi group.

editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(K\) be a perfect field of characteristic \(\neq 2\), let \(P(x)\in K[x]\), and let \(a\) be the discriminant of \(P(x)\). Suppose that \(P(x)\) is an irreducible polynomial of degree 3 with symmetric Galois group and that \(a\neq b^2\) for \(b\in K\). Let \(X\) be the affine surface defined over \(K\) by the equation \(y^2-az^2 = P(x)\) and let \(Y\) be the threefold defined over \(k\), for \(K = k(t)\), by the same equation. Suppose, moreover, that the field \(k\) is algebraically closed. Under these assumptions, \textit{A. Beauville, J.-L. Colliot-Théléne, J.-J. Sansuc}, and \textit{P. Swinnerton-Dyer} [Ann. Math. (2) 121, 283--318 (1985; Zbl 0589.14042)] proved that the variety \(X\) (respectively \(Y\)) is not \(K\)-rational (respectively not \(k\)-rational), but \(X\times \mathbb{A}^3_K\) is \(K\)-rational and \(Y\times \mathbb{A}^3_k\) is \(k\)-rational. Improving on their results, the author proves that already \(X\times \mathbb{A}^2_K\) is \(K\)-rational and \(Y\times \mathbb{A}^2_k\) is \(k\)-rational.

editorial_contributions.text: A variety \(X\) is called rational if it is birational to projective space, and stably rational if \(X \times \mathbb P^r\) is rational for some \(r\). This paper is about the behavior of stable rationality in families of varieties. The authors exhibit a family of smooth projective complex \(3\)-folds such that there is a stably rational member, but the very general member is not stably rational. This phenomenon was previously known to exist in dimensions \(\ge 4\) (even with a rational member). The question whether one can have both rational and non-stably rational members in dimension \(3\) remains open.

This is a survey of numerous results obtained so far on the rationality or stable rationality of the various function fields arising from moduli problems in algebraic geometry. 


Let \(G\) be an affine algebraic group acting linearly on a complex vector space \(V\) of finite dimension. A central problem discussed in this article is whether or not the field of \(G\)-invariants \({\mathbb{C}}(V)^ G\) is rational over \({\mathbb{C}}\). The author summarizes the known positive (sometimes negative) results by means of the methods used in the proofs. Then he turns to discussions of the rationality of the moduli spaces which are birationally equivalent to the orbit spaces of the type \({\mathbb{P}}(V)/G\).

editorial_contributions.text:
A smooth projective variety \(X\) defined over an algebraically closed field \(k\) is called stably rational if and only if \(X \times \mathbb{P}^n_k\) is rational, for some \(n>0\). A breakthrough in the problem of studying the stable rationality of varieties was achieved by \textit{C. Voisin} [Invent. Math. 201, No. 1, 207--237 (2015; Zbl 1327.14223)] who obtained a criterion for the general member of a family of varieties to fail be stably rational.

In this paper the authors study the stable rationality of Brauer-Severi surface bundles, a higher dimensional generalization of conic bundles.

A Brauer-Severi surface bundle, is a flat projective morphisms \(f : X \rightarrow S\) between smooth projective varieties over a perfect field of characteristic different than 3 such that the fiber over any geometric point of \(S\) is one of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item[1.] A Del Pezzo surface of degree 9,
\item[2.] The union of three Hirzebruch surfaces \(\mathbb{F}_1\) meeting transversally such that any pair of them meets along a fiber of one and the \((-1)\)-curve of the other,
\item[3.] An irreducible scheme whose underlying reduced subscheme is isomorphic to the cone over a twisted cubic curve.
\end{itemize}

In this paper the authors prove the following. Let \(S\) be a rational smooth projective surface over an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic different than 3 and \(L\) a very ample line bundle on \(S\) such that the linear system \(|L|\) contains a nodal reducible curve \(D=D_1\cup D_2\), where \(D_1, D_2\) are smooth with positive genus and contains also a curve with \(E_6\)-singularity. If the base field has positive characteristic, it is also assumed that \(H^1(S,L)=0\) and that some curve in \(|L|\) with \(E_6\)-singularity can be lifted with \(S\) and \(L\) to characteristic zero. Then the Brauer-Severi surface bundle corresponding to a very general element of \(|L|\) with nontrivial cyclic degree 3 cover is not stably rational.

The main idea of the proof of the previous result is to construct a family of Brauer-Severi surface bundles such that one member has an obstruction to stable rationality and and then conclude by the method developed by C. Voisin [loc. cit.] that the very general member of the family is not stably rational.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: We prove that a very general hypersurface of bidegree \((2,n)\) in \(\mathbb{P}^2\times\mathbb{P}^2\) for \(n\) bigger than or equal to 2 is not stably rational, using \textit{C. Voisin}'s [Invent. Math. 201, No. 1, 207--237 (2015; Zbl 1327.14223)] method of integral Chow-theoretic decompositions of the diagonal and their preservation under mild degenerations. At the same time, we also analyse possible ways to degenerate Prym curves, and the way how various loci inside the moduli space of stable Prym curves are nested. No deformation theory of stacks or sheaves of Azumaya algebras like in recent work of Hassett-Kresch-Tschinkel [\textit{B. Hassett} et al., Math. Ann. 365, No. 3--4, 1201--1217 (2016; Zbl 1353.14019); \textit{B. Hassett} and \textit{Y. Tschinkel}, ``On stable rationality of Fano threefolds and del Pezzo fibrations'', Preprint, \url{arXiv:1601.07074}] is used, rather we employ a more elementary and explicit approach via Koszul complexes, which is enough to treat this special case.

title.title: On stable rationality of some conic bundles and moduli spaces of Prym curves

editorial_contributions.text:
A variety over a field \(k\) is {\em stably rational} if some field of rational functions in finitely many variables over its function field is isomorphic over \(k\) to a field of rational functions over \(k\). In the present paper, the authors prove that a very general hypersurface of bidegree \((2,3)\) in \(\mathbb P^2\times \mathbb P^3\) over \(\mathbb C\) is not stably rational, and also produce loci of rational hypersurfaces of this bidegree. This settles the last open case of hypersurfaces of \(\mathbb P^2\times \mathbb P^3\) of bidegrees \((2,d)\) and \((e,3)\), \(d,e\geq 2\); all very general such hypersurfaces are now known not to be stably rational. The case of bidegree \((2,2)\) was previously proved by \textit{B. Hassett} et al. [Acta Math. 220, No. 2, 341--365 (2018; Zbl 1420.14115)] and the cases of \(d\geq 4\) or \(e\geq 3\) were previously settled by \textit{H. Ahmadinezhad} and \textit{T. Okada} [Épijournal de Géom. Algébr., EPIGA 2, Article No. 5, 13 p. (2018; Zbl 1422.14022)] and \textit{I. Krylov} and \textit{T. Okada} [``Stable rationality of del Pezzo fibrations of low degree over projective spaces'', Preprint, \url{arXiv:1701.08372}]. 

The authors of the present paper use the method of the papers by \textit{C. Voisin} [Invent. Math. 201, No. 1, 207--237 (2015; Zbl 1327.14223)] and \textit{J.-L. Colliot-Thélène} and \textit{A. Pirutka} [Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. (4) 49, No. 2, 371--397 (2016; Zbl 1371.14028)], which applies to generically smooth projective morphisms \(X\to B\) with positive-dimensional fibers where \(B\) is a quasiprojective variety over an algebraically closed field. If there is a closed point of \(B\) whose fiber is not universally \(CH_0\)-trivial but admits a proper universally \(CH_0\)-trivial resolution of singularities, then the fiber of a very general closed point of \(B\) is not stably rational. Here one says that a proper variety is {\em universally \(CH_0\)-trivial} if its \(0\)-dimensional algebraic cycles over any field extension are classified under rational equivalence just by their degree. In addition to using this method, the authors also further develop it, proving a number of technical results.

As another application of their methods, the authors also produce a smooth cubic surface \(X\) over \(\mathbb C(x,y)\) such that the 
cokernel of the canonical map from the Brauer group of \(\mathbb C(x,y)\) to the Brauer group of \(X\) contains a nontrivial \(2\)-torsion class which is unramified on any fourfold model of \(X\).

title.title: On the local zeta function of a cubic threefold

editorial_contributions.text:
The authors study higher dimensional hyperelliptic Jacobians and the isogeny classes thereof. For example, they prove that such a very general hyperelliptic Jacobian, of dimension at least four, is isogenous to no non-hyperelliptic Jacobian. Furthermore, the authors establish that the intermediate Jacobian of a very general cubic threefold is not isogenous to a Jacobian.

In a related direction, the authors study closed subvarieties of \(\mathcal{A}_g\) the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension \(g \geq 3\). Among other results, they prove that if a very general element of such a subvariety \(\mathcal{Y}\), with \(\dim \mathcal{Y} \geq 3\), is dominated by the Jacobian of a curve, then this curve is not hyperelliptic.

One point in the proof of these results involves the study of étale surjective maps between certain generalized Jacobians. Such morphisms arise as the limit of suitably defined families of isogenies of Jacobians.

title.title: Hyperelliptic Jacobians and isogenies

editorial_contributions.text:
This paper decomposes up to isogeny the intermediate Jacobians of a special type of cubic threefolds. Let \(X\) be a smooth cubic threefold defined over \(\mathbb{C}\) admitting an automorphism of order five. Such cubic threefolds are described in [\textit{V. González-Aguilera} and \textit{A. Liendo}, Arch. Math. 97, No. 1, 25--37 (2011; Zbl 1231.14033)] using explicit equations. The main result of this paper is that the intermediate Jacobian \(J(X)\) of \(X\) is isogenous to \(E\times B^2\), where \(E\) is an elliptic curve and \(B\) is an abelian surface with real multiplication by \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})\), i.e. \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})\subset\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb{C}}(B)\otimes_{\mathbb Z} \mathbb{Q}\). Furthermore, the authors shows that the same conclusion also holds for \(X\) defined over any field \(k\) of characteristic zero containing a primitive fifth root of unity.

Following \textit{J. P. Murre} [Compos. Math. 25, 161--206 (1972; Zbl 0242.14002)], the authors construct explicitly from \(X\) an algebraic curve \(\mathcal H_l\) with an involution \(\iota_l\), so that the Prym variety associated to the double cover \(\mathcal H_l\to\mathcal H_l/\iota_l\) is the intermediate Jacobian \(J(X)\). Under this geometric interpretation of \(J(X)\), the authors are able to construct concrete models of its elliptic component \(E\) and its abelian surface component \(B\) up to isogeny.

The proofs and the constructions in this paper are explicit and hence very accessible to readers.

title.title: On intermediate Jacobians of cubic threefolds admitting an automorphism of order five

editorial_contributions.text:
In this paper, the author manages to say something new about the twenty-seven lines on a cubic surface.

The main object of interest is the abelian fivefold \(Q(Y)\) associated with a cubic surface \(Y\): essentially this is the intermediate Jacobian of the cubic threefold \(Z\) obtained by taking the triple cover of \({\mathbb P}^3\) ramified exactly along \(Y\). By means of a Prym construction one may do this not just complex-analytically but over \({\text{Spec}}\, {\mathbb Z}[1/6]\), as shown by the author in [Zbl 1325.14053]. The abelian fivefolds that arise have an action of the Eisenstein integers of signature \((4,1)\) and are principally polarised. The idea here is to study the moduli space of stable cubic surfaces via this correspondence, thus exploiting the theory of Shimura varieties.

Two distinct kinds of result are shown here. Over the complex numbers, the author calculates all the possible Hodge groups (and Mumford-Tate groups) of the abelian fivefolds \(Q(Y)\), showing that they do all occur. In fact the Mumford-Tate groups are determined by the endomorphism algebras, and it is these that are classified. It is quite delicate to show that one may obtain the desired endomorphism algebra (which is an isogeny invariant) exactly while still retaining principal polarisation.

On the other hand, one can ask about the monodromy groups of the universal abelian fivefold pulled back to the moduli of cubic surfaces. Over the complex numbers this is quite well understood, but here, by careful use of some rather general monodromy calculations for unitary Shimura varieties, the calculation is carried out (\(\ell\)-adically) over more or less arbitrary fields (with some limitations at \(2\) and \(3\)). In particular, it is shown that the Galois group of the field of definition of the \(27\) lines on a cubic surface over a field \(K\) of characteristic prime to \(6\) is usually \(W(E_6)\): for the complex numbers, this is a modern rephrasing of a result of Jordan from 1870.

title.title: Abelian varieties with no power isogenous to a Jacobian

editorial_contributions.text:
The paper is concerned with proving a global and an infinitesimal Torelli theorem for smooth cubic threefolds with certain involutions. Automorphisms of cubic threefolds induce automorphisms on the associated intermediate Jacobian. Of these, involutions are especially well-understood. There are two types of involutions, Eckardt type and non-Eckardt type. The former was studied in [\textit{S. Casalaina-Martin} and \textit{Z. Zhang}, J. Lond. Math. Soc., II. Ser. 104, No. 1, 1--34 (2021; Zbl 1494.14026)] where they also established a Torelli theorem, in particular, a way to recover the cubic threefold with the involution from the invariant piece of the Jacobian split off by the induced involution.

The starting point of this paper is the classical fact that cubic threefolds can be recovered from the associated conic bundle obtained by the projection from a general line. Such a conic bundle induces a 2:1 étale map between a curve of genus 11 and the discriminant curve, which is planar of genus 6. A non-Eckardt type involution fixes a line on the cubic. This line, albeit not general, gives rise to a conic bundle whose discriminant consists of a smooth planar cubic curve \(C\) and a conic. This elliptic curve \(C\), in fact, lies on the cubic itself and is fixed by the involution. The associated double cover of this reducible plane quintic is again reducible and induces a double cover \(\widetilde{C}\to C\) branched at the six intersections points between \(C\) and the conic. Theorem 2.5 shows that the dual of the Prym associated to this ramified double cover splits off from the intermediate Jacobian of \(Y\), up to isogeny. This Prym is a \((1,2,2)\)-polarised abelian variety. Furthermore, it induces an injective map from the moduli space of degree 2 cover of elliptic curves ramified at 6 points to the moduli space of \((1,2,2)\)-polarised abelian varieties. Therefore, it suffices to reconstruct the cubic together with the involution from the data of this double cover. More precisely, the reconstruction of the cubic threefold along with the involution is performed in Theorem 3.2: The data \((C, \beta, \mathcal{L}, s)\) of the smooth planar elliptic curve \(C\), a divisor \(\beta\) and a line bundle \(\mathcal{L}\), such that \(\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 2}\simeq \mathcal{O}_C(\beta)\) and a section \(s\in H^0(C, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes 2})\) vanishing along \(\beta\) recovers a unique smooth cubic threefold \(Y\) with a non-Eckardt type involution. The key ingredient is to observe that \(H^2(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}(2)) \simeq H^2(C, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes 2})\), i.e., the section \(s\) uniquely determines a conic \(Q\) so that \(Q\cap C = \beta\). From this data they construct the conic bundle and the involution explicitly and check that the projection from the fixed line induces the desired discriminant \(C\cup Q\) and its unique double cover branched at the intersection points.

They show an infinitesimal Torelli as well. This holds over the open locus of cubic threefolds with non-Eckardt type involutions such that the associated conic in the discriminant is smooth. In a slightly different direction, they analyse the effect of projecting such cubic threefolds from a general line.

title.title: On the automorphism group of a certain cubic threefold

editorial_contributions.text:
The set of lines on a smooth cubic threefold \(F\) is parametrized by the so-called Fano surface of the threefold, a surface embedded in the intermediate Jacobian of \(F\) by its own Albanese morphism.

The Tangent Bundle Theorem enables to recover the cubic from its Fano surface. The author had previousy proved [Manuscr. Math. 129, No. 3, 381--399 (2009; Zbl 1177.14079)] that the automorphism group of the threefold is isomorphic to the automorphism group of its Fano surface.

In this paper he pursue the study of these groups. He first proves that the order of this group divides \(11\cdot 7 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 3^{6} \cdot 2^{23}\). Then he shows that a smooth cubic threefold cannot have an automorphism of order \(7\), and the the only cubic threefold with an automorphism of order \(11\) is the Klein cubic 
\[
x_1x_5^2+x_5x_3^2+x_3x_4^2+x_4x_2^2+x_2x_1^2=0.
\]
 The automorphism group of the Klein cubic is isomorphic to \(PSL(2,11)\), as shown by \textit{A. Adler} [J. Algebra 72, 146--165 (1981; Zbl 0479.20020)]. Using that, the author computes the period lattice of the Fano surface of the Klein cubic, the rank and the discriminant of its Néron-Severi group. He computes also the numerical classes of all connected fibrations of the Fano surface onto a curve of positive genus.

title.title: The Fano surface of the Klein cubic threefold

editorial_contributions.text:
This paper investigates period maps for smooth projective hypersurfaces through partial Fermat structures. Applications include cubic surfaces and threefolds.

As a preparation the author determines the integral polarised Hodge structure of the primitive middle cohomology of a Fermat variety. Here it is considered as a module over the automorphism group of the polarized hypersurface. Previously this seems to have been known only over \(\mathbb{Q}\).

The main technique of the paper is to enhance a hypersurface of degree \(d\) by adding a partial Fermat structure consisting of one or more new variables raised to the \(d\)th power. The author determines the impact on the period maps.

Specifically the author works out the application to cubics. From the analysis of cubic fourfolds, done independently by R. Laza and the author, he derives complete information about the period maps of cubic surfaces and threefolds, thus recovering results of Allcock-Carlson-Toledo.

For the entire collection see [Zbl 1193.14002].

title.title: Fermat varieties and the periods of some hypersurfaces

editorial_contributions.text:
Summary: We characterise smooth curves in a smooth cubic threefold whose blow-ups produce a weak-Fano threefold. These are curves \(C\) of genus \(g\) and degree \(d\), such that (i) \(2(d-5)\leq g\) and \(d\leq 6\); (ii) \(C\) does not admit a 3-secant line in the cubic threefold. Among the list of ten possible such types \((g,d)\), two yield Sarkisov links that are birational selfmaps of the cubic threefold, namely \((g,d)=(0,5)\)
and \((2,6)\). Using the link associated with a curve of type \((2,6)\), we are able to produce the first example of a pseudo-automorphism with dynamical degree greater than 1 on a smooth threefold with Picard number 3. We also prove that the group of birational selfmaps of any smooth cubic threefold contains elements contracting surfaces birational to any given ruled surface.

editorial_contributions.text:
A Fano surface is the Hilbert scheme of lines of a smooth cubic threefold of \(\mathbb P^4\). It is a smooth surface of general type with irregularity \(5\) and globally generated cotangent sheaf.

The author studied [Geom. Dedicata 142, 151--171 (2009; Zbl 1180.14041)] the cotangent map of these surfaces. In this paper he investigates the elliptic curves contained in a Fano surface.

The elliptic curves in a surface of general type are an obstruction for the ampleness of the cotangent sheaf, and in the case of Fano surfaces these curves are proved here to be the only obstruction. All the possible configurations of such curves are classified, i.e. their intersection matrix and a plane model of any of them are determined. Moreover, the author constructs a subgroup of the automorphism group of the surface which classifies completely these configurations.

The number of such curves is related to the Picard number. These results, as the author notes in the Introduction, imply that the ampleness of the cotangent bundle, and the geometric properties of the cotangent map, vary non-trivially in the moduli space of Fano surfaces.

Eventually the author applies is knowledge of Fano surfaces to construct a cubic threefold whose intermediate Jacobian is isomorphic -- as a polarized abelian variety -- to a product of elliptic curves.

title.title: Automorphisms of singular three-dimensional cubic hypersurfaces

editorial_contributions.text:
The authors show that the moduli space of nodal cubic surfaces is isomorphic to a quotient of a 4-dimensional complex ball by an arithmetic subgroup of the unitary group given as corollary 9.3 of the main theorem 9.2 of this paper. A similar uniformization is given for different covers of the moduli space corresponding to geometric markings of the Picard Group or a choice of a line on the surface. Their construction and most of their results in this direction are related to the work of \textit{D. Allcock} et al. [J. Algebr. Geom. 11, 659--724 (2002; Zbl 1080.14532)] and \textit{K. Matsumoto} et al. [ J. Algebr. Geom. 3, 741--775 (2003; Zbl 1048.14027)]. 

Their paper is organized as follows. In section 2 they study stable cubic surfaces, referred here as nodal cubic surfaces. In section 2.1 they define markings of nodal cubic surfaces and introduce the moduli space of marked nodal cubic surfaces \({M^m}_{\text{ncub}}\), which admits a natural compactification and discuss different constructions of this compactification in sections 2.8--2.10. For a nodal cubic surface and a line on it they define in section 3 a pair of binary forms, of degree 2 and 5 modulo the action of SL(2). Using this they prove in corollary 3.8 to proposition 3.6 that the moduli space of cubic surfaces together with a choice of a line on it is a rational variety. In section 4, the authors define a \(K3\) surface \(X_{S,l}\), which by theorem 4.9 depends only on \(S\), henceforth denoted as \(X_S\). They relate the \(K3\) surface \(X_S\) to the associated cubic fourfold with a plane to the cubic threefold \(V\) corresponding to \(S\) by Allcock et al. [loc.cit ] in section 4.15 and to a curve called by the authors the ``Matsumoto-Terasoma'' curve \(C\) in remark 4.16. In section 5 the authors show that the Picard lattice of a generic \(X_S\) is isomorphic to the lattice \(M= U \oplus{ A_2}^{\oplus 5} \). The lattice of transcendental cycles is isomorphic to the lattice \( A_2(-1) {\oplus}{ A_2}^{\oplus 4} \) as shown in proposition 5.3. 

In section 6 they study the moduli space of \(M\)-polarized \(K3\) surfaces \((X, \phi:M \rightarrow \text{Pic}(X))\). They show that by explicitly describing an isometry \(\rho\) on the orthogonal complement of \(\phi(M)\) in \( H^2(X_S,Z)\) that the image of the period map of the surfaces \(X_S\) lies in the fixed locus of a certain automorphism of order 3 on the period space of \(M\)-polarized \(K3\) surfaces. They construct in this way in section 6.14 the moduli space \( {K3^m}_{M, \rho} \) of \((M, \rho)\)-polarized \(K3\) surfaces as a quotient of \(B\) (see section 6.7 for the explicite definition). In section 7, they establish a natural \(W(E_6)\)-equivariant isomorphism from the moduli space of marked nonsingular cubic surfaces \({M^m}_{\text{cub}}\) onto an open subset \({K3^m}_{M, \rho}- {\Delta}^m \) in the theorem of subsection 7.2. 

In section 8 they study in detail the geometry of the discriminant locus \(\Delta^m \). editorial_contributions.text:
This paper decomposes up to isogeny the intermediate Jacobians of a special type of cubic threefolds. Let \(X\) be a smooth cubic threefold defined over \(\mathbb{C}\) admitting an automorphism of order five. Such cubic threefolds are described in [\textit{V. González-Aguilera} and \textit{A. Liendo}, Arch. Math. 97, No. 1, 25--37 (2011; Zbl 1231.14033)] using explicit equations. The main result of this paper is that the intermediate Jacobian \(J(X)\) of \(X\) is isogenous to \(E\times B^2\), where \(E\) is an elliptic curve and \(B\) is an abelian surface with real multiplication by \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})\), i.e. \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})\subset\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb{C}}(B)\otimes_{\mathbb Z} \mathbb{Q}\). Furthermore, the authors shows that the same conclusion also holds for \(X\) defined over any field \(k\) of characteristic zero containing a primitive fifth root of unity.

Following \textit{J. P. Murre} [Compos. Math. 25, 161--206 (1972; Zbl 0242.14002)], the authors construct explicitly from \(X\) an algebraic curve \(\mathcal H_l\) with an involution \(\iota_l\), so that the Prym variety associated to the double cover \(\mathcal H_l\to\mathcal H_l/\iota_l\) is the intermediate Jacobian \(J(X)\). Under this geometric interpretation of \(J(X)\), the authors are able to construct concrete models of its elliptic component \(E\) and its abelian surface component \(B\) up to isogeny.

The proofs and the constructions in this paper are explicit and hence very accessible to readers.

editorial_contributions.text: The paper under review is concerned with affine analogues of the classical projective notions of birationally (uni-)ruled varieties. Let \(X\) be a complex quasi-projective variety. One says that \(X\) is \(\mathbb A^1\)-ruled if it contains a Zariski dense open subset of the form \(U \simeq \mathbb A^1 \times Y\). On the other hand \(X\) is \(\mathbb A^1\)-uniruled if it contains a Zariski dense open subset \(U\) such that any \(x \in U\) is contained in the image of a non constant morphism \(f_x : \mathbb A^1 \to X\). The main result of the paper asserts that for any smooth hypersurface \(Z_n \subset \mathbb P^n\) of degree \(n \geq 3\), the affine variety \(X = \mathbb P^n \setminus Z_n\) is \(\mathbb A^1\)-uniruled but not \(\mathbb A^1\)-ruled. The proof in the case \(n \geq 4\) uses the fact that \(Z_n\) is then birationally rigid [\textit{T. de Fernex}, Invent. Math. 192, No. 3, 533--566 (2013; Zbl 1279.14019)], and so in particular cannot be a component of the exceptional locus of any birational map. The proof in dimension \(n = 3\) relies on a different argument, namely the fact that a smooth projective cubic threefold is not rational [\textit{C. H. Clemens} and \textit{P. A. Griffiths}, Ann. Math. (2) 95, 281--356 (1972; Zbl 0214.48302)]. The last part of the paper is a step towards the open question whether the complement \(X\) of a smooth cubic surface in \(\mathbb P^3\) might admit automorphisms that are not induced by linear automorphisms of the ambient \(\mathbb P^3\). The authors study some fibrations on \(X\), corresponding to ``special pencils'' whose general elements are smooth cubic surfaces minus a conic and a tangent line, or minus three lines meeting at a Eckardt point. Each such fiber admits an involution of Geiser type, but all these involutions do not fit into a global automorphism of \(X\), and more generally the authors prove that any automorphism of such a special pencil is the restriction of a linear automorphism (hence is trivial for a generic \(Z_3\)).

editorial_contributions.text:
In this paper the authors construct an explicit smooth Fano complex threefold with Picard number \(1\), index \(1\) and degree \(10\) known as Gushel-Mukai threefold, and they prove it is not rational by showing it has a faithful \(\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_{11})\)-action.

\textit{A. Beauville} [Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. (4) 10, 309--391 (1977; Zbl 0368.14018)] proved that a general Fano threefold with Picard number \(1\), index \(1\) and degree 10 (also known as a Gushel-Mukai threefold) is irrational, but no smooth examples are known. Here they construct a complete 2-dimensional family of such examples (Corollary 5.3) including one such threefold defined over \(\mathbb{Q}\) by explicit equations (Corollary 5.4).

The starting point of the paper is an EPW-sextic with a faithful \(\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_{11})\)-action discovered by Mongardi in 2013. Starting from this famous sextic hypersurface \(Y_{\mathbb{A}} \subset \mathbb{P}^5\) with a faithful action of a simple group \(\mathbb{G}:= \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{F}_{11})\) they prove that \(\Aut(Y_{\mathbb{A}})=\mathbb{G}\) (Proposition 4.1) and this is the only quasi smooth EPW sextic with an automorphism of order \(11\) (Theorem 4.2).

Along the way they construct Gushel-Mukai varieties of various dimensions with large (finite) automorphism groups. By [\textit{O. Debarre} and \textit{A. Kuznetsov}, Épijournal de Géom. Algébr., EPIGA 4, Article 19, 45 p. (2020; Zbl 1457.14092)] the intermediate Jacobians of Gushel-Mukai varieties obtained from the sextic \(Y_{\mathbb{A}}\) are all isomorphic to a principally polarized abelian variety \((\mathbb{J}, \theta)\). They use the Clemens-Griffiths [\textit{C. H. Clemens} and \textit{P. A. Griffiths}, Ann. Math. (2) 95, 281--356 (1972; Zbl 0214.48302)] criterion to prove that the GM threefolds that they construct from \(Y_{\mathbb{A}}\) are not rational. To apply the criterion it is enough to prove that their (common) intermediate Jacobian \((\mathbb{J}, \theta)\) is not a product of Jacobians of curves and to get this, they use the fact that \((\mathbb{J}, \theta)\) has too many automorphisms (because of the \(\mathbb{G}\)-action). This is how they produce a complete 2-dimensional family of irrational GM threefolds, all mutually birationally isomorphic.

Moreover another important object that the authors study in the paper is the 10-dimensional principally polarized abelian variety \((\mathbb{J}, \theta)\). They get that this abelian variety is indecomposable and isogenous to the product of ten copies of an elliptic curve (Proposition 5.1 and 5.8) and they conjecture that this variety is isomorphic to an explicit 10 dimensional principally polarized abelian variety (see the construction in Proposition C.3). Since this situation is quite similar to the one of the Klein cubic threefold \(W \subset \mathbb{P}^4\), they call the sextic \(Y_{\mathbb{A}}\), the Klein EPW sextic.

Finally it is remarkable to recall that the proofs heavily use the construction by \textit{K. G. O'Grady} [Mich. Math. J. 62, No. 1, 143--184 (2013; Zbl 1276.14008)] of canonical double covers of quasi-smooth EPW sextics called double EPW sextics [\textit{O. Debarre} and \textit{A. Kuznetsov}, Math. Ann. 378, No. 3--4, 1435--1469 (2020; Zbl 1468.14027)].

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Let $Y$ be a cubic threefold with a non-Eckardt type involution $\tau$. Our first main result is that the $\tau$-equivariant category of the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(Y)$ determines the isomorphism class of $Y$ for general $(Y,\tau)$. We shall prove this categorical Torelli theorem via three approaches: a noncommutative Hodge theoretical one (using a generalization of the intermediate Jacobian construction due to Alexander Perry), a Bridgeland moduli theoretical one (using equivariant stability conditions), and a Chow theoretical one (using some techniques in [kuznetsovnonclodedfield2021]).The remaining part of the paper is devoted to proving an equivariant infinitesimal categorical Torelli for non-Eckardt cubic threefolds $(Y,\tau)$. To accomplish it, we prove a compatibility theorem on the algebra structures of the Hochschild cohomology of the bounded derived category $D^b(X)$ of a smooth projective variety $X$ and on the Hochschild cohomology of a semi-orthogonal component of $D^b(X)$. Another key ingredient is a generalization of a result in [macri2009infinitesima] which shows that the twisted Hochschild-Kostant-Rosenberg isomorphism is compatible with the actions on the Hochschild cohomology and on the singular cohomology induced by an automorphism of $X$. In appendix, we prove an equivariant categorical Torelli theorem for arbitrary cubic threefold with a geometric involution under a natural assumption.

The paper under review deals with Fano surfaces \(S\) with a non-trivial automorphism group and their quotients.

The main tools used in this study are the computation of invariants on quotients, intersection theory on normal surfaces and the properties of the smooth cubic threefold whose lines are parametrized by \(S\).

All the possible cases are examined: cyclic groups of order 2,3,4,5,11,15 and non-cyclic groups \((\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2\), \(\mathbb D_2\), \((\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z)^2\), \(\mathcal S_3\), \(\mathbb D_3\), \(\mathbb D_5\) and \(G\) (a group generated by two involution of type I whose product has order 3 and a type III(1) automorphism). For each group the quotient singularities and the main invariants are explicitly determined.

Anal. 11, No. 1, 135--160 (2001; Zbl 0994.32019)] to describe precisely when an automorphism group of a complex manifolds is ``large''. The Andersen-Lempert Theorem [\textit{E. Andersén} and \textit{L. Lempert}, Invent. Math. 110, No. 2, 371--388 (1992; Zbl 0770.32015); \textit{F. Forstnerič} and \textit{J.-P. Rosay}, Invent. Math. 112, No. 2, 323--349 (1993; Zbl 0792.32011)], which is essentially a Runge-type approximation theorem for holomorphic automorphisms, can then be generalized from the complex-Euclidean space to Stein manifolds with the density property.

A complex manifold \(X\) enjoys the density property if the Lie algebra generated by its complete holomorphic vector fields is dense in the Lie algebra of all of its holomorphic vector fields. Moreover, if there exists a nowhere vanishing section \(\omega\) of the canonical bundle of \(X\), then one can define also the following property: \((X, \omega)\) enjoys the volume density property if the Lie algebra generated by its complete \(\omega\)-preserving holomorphic vector fields is dense in the Lie algebra of all of its \(\omega\)-preserving holomorphic vector fields.

In this paper, the author establishes the density property for a family of Stein manifolds given by \(X := \{x^2 y = a + x b\} \subset \mathbb{C}_x \times \mathbb{C}_y \times \mathbb{C}_z^{n+1}\) with \(a\) and \(b\) being certain polynomials in \(z\), as well as the volume density property for these manifolds w.r.t. the holomorphic volume form \(dx/x^2 \wedge dz\). As the most interesting example, it includes the well-known Koras-Russell cubic \(x^2 y = -(z_0^2 + z_1^3) - x\) which is known to be diffeomorphic to \(\mathbb R^6\) but not algebraically isomorphic to \(\mathbb C^3\).

editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(S\) be a smooth projective surface with ample canonical bundle and let \(D\) be a reduced simple normal crossing divisor on \(S\) (maybe \(D=0\)). It is a well known fact that the (logarithmic) Chern numbers \(\overline{c}^2_1\) and \(\overline{c}_2\) of \(S'=S-D\) satisfy 
\[
 \overline{c}^2_1\leq3\overline{c}_2\,,
\]
 and the equality holds if and only if \(S'\) is a ball quotient. Few constructions of surfaces with Chern ratio \(\frac{\overline{c}^2_1}{\overline{c}_2}=3\) are known.

In the paper under review, the author considers the Fano surface \(S\) (which is a surface of general type) parameterizing lines on the Fermat cubic threefold. He shows that the divisor \(D\) consists of \(12\) disjoint elliptic curves and that \(S'\) is a ball quotient with log Chern numbers \(\overline{c}_1^2=3\overline{c}_2=3^4\).

Using a result of [\textit{M. Namba}, Branched coverings and algebraic functions. Pitman Research Notes in Mathematics Series, 161. Harlow: Longman Scientific \& Technical; New York: John Wiley \& Sons Ltd. (1987; Zbl 0706.14017)] the author proves that there exist a degree \(3^4\) ramified cover \(\eta: S\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_1\) branched with order 3 over the ten \((-1)\)-curves of \(\mathcal{H}_1\), the del Pezzo surface of degree 5. Moreover, there exists an étale map \(\kappa: \mathcal{H}_3\rightarrow S\) that is a quotient of \(\mathcal{H}_3\) by an automorphism of order 3, where \(\eta_3: \mathcal{H}_3\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_1\) is a degree \(3^5\) cover branched over the ten \((-1)\)-curves of \(\mathcal{H}_1\) with order \(3\) constructed by \textit{F. Hirzebruch} [Progr. Math. 36, 113--140 (1983; Zbl 0527.14033)].

In analogy with a result of \textit{T. Yamazaki} and \textit{M. Yoshida} [Math. Ann. 266, 421--431 (1984; Zbl 0513.14008)], the author shows that the surface \(\mathcal{T}=\kappa^{-1}S' \subset \mathcal{H}_3\) is a ball quotient: \(\mathcal{T}\cong \mathbb{B}_2/\Lambda\), where \(\Lambda\) is the commutator group of the Deligne-Mostow lattice associated to the \(5\)-tuple \((1/3,1/3,1/3,1/3,2/3)\) [\textit{P. Deligne} and \textit{G. D. Mostow}, Publ. Math., Inst. Hautes Étud. Sci. 63, 5--89 (1986; Zbl 0615.22008)].

editorial_contributions.text:
The article under review reflects the content of the course ``Prym Varieties'', delivered by the authors at the Trieste Algebraic Summer School in 2021.

After the first introductory section, the second one recalls some basic notions and properties of the abelian varieties. More precisely, it discusses briefly the Jacobian \(JC\) of a smooth curve \(C\) of genus \(g \geq 1, \) the Abel-Jacobi map \(\alpha : \mathrm{Div} ^0 (C) \rightarrow \mathrm{Pic} ^0 (C) = JC\) of the divisors \(\mathrm{Div} ^0 (C)\) of degree \(0\) in the Picard group \(\mathrm{Pic} ^0 (C)\) of the line bundles of degree \(0\), the moduli space \(\mathcal{A}_g\) of the principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension \(g, \) the moduli space \(\mathcal{M} _g\) of the smooth projective curves of genus \(g > 1, \) the Torelli map \(\mathfrak{t}: \mathcal{M} _g \rightarrow \mathcal{A} _g\) and the theta divisor \(W _{g-1} \subset \mathrm{Pic} ^{g-1} (C)\) in the set \(\mathrm{Pic} ^{g-1} (C)\) of the line bundles of degre \(g-1\).

The next, third section introduces the Prym variety \(P( \pi) \subset J \widetilde{C}\) of a finite covering \(\pi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\) of smooth projective curves. More precisely, if \(\mathrm{Nm} _{\pi} : J \widetilde{C} \rightarrow JC, \) \(\mathrm{Nm} _{\pi} \widetilde{\alpha} \left( \sum\limits _i n_i p_i \right) := \alpha \left( \sum\limits _i n_i \pi ( p_i) \right), \) \(\forall \sum _i n_i p_i \in\mathrm{Div} ^0 ( \widetilde{C})\) is the norm map of \(\pi\) then \(P ( \pi)\) is the identity component of the kernel of \(\mathrm{Nm} _{\pi}. \) The moduli space \(\mathcal{R}_g := \{ [ C, \eta] \, \vert \, [C] \in \mathcal{M} _g, \, \eta \in\mathrm{Pic} ^0 (C) \setminus \{ \mathcal{O}_C \}, \, \eta ^{ \otimes 2} = \mathcal{O}_C \}\) of the étale double coverings \(\pi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\) of the curves \(C\) of genus \(g\) has a Prym map \(\mathcal{P}_g : \mathcal{R}_g \rightarrow \mathcal{A}_{g-1}, \) \(\mathcal{P}_g ( [ C, \eta])= ( P ( \pi), \widetilde{\Theta} \vert _{P ( \pi)} ),\) which associates to \(\pi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\) its Prym variety \(P ( \pi)\) with the polarization \(\widetilde{\Theta} \vert _{P ( \pi)}, \) induced by the principal polarization \(\widetilde{\Theta}\) of \(J \widetilde{C}. \) This section discusses the dominance of \(\mathcal{P}_g\) for \(g \leq 6\), the generic injectiveness of \(\mathcal{P}_g\) for \(g \geq 7\) and the fact that \(\mathcal{P}_g\) is never globally injective.

The remaining seven sections are devoted to the fibres of the Prym map \(\mathcal{P}_6 : \mathcal{R}_6 \rightarrow \mathcal{A}_5. \)

The fourth section discusses how the Prym map \( \mathcal{P}_g : \mathcal{R}_g \rightarrow \mathcal{A}_{g-1}\) extends to a proper map \(\overline{\mathcal{P}_g} : \overline{\mathcal{R}_g} \rightarrow \mathcal{A}_{g-1}\) on the moduli space \(\overline{\mathcal{R}_g}\) of the allowable covers. Let us recall that a complete connected curve \(C\) is stable if it has at most ordinary double points and a finite automorphism group. If \(\overline{\mathcal{M}_g}\) and \(\overline{\mathcal{M}_{2g-1}}\) are the compactifications of \(\mathcal{M}_g, \) respectively, \(\mathcal{M}_{2g-1}\) by the stable curves then a double covering \(\pi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\) of \(C \in \overline{\mathcal{M}_g}\) by \( \widetilde{C} \in \overline{\mathcal{M}_{2g-1}}\) is allowable if its associated Prym variety is an abelian variety.

The fifth section constructs a strategy for computing the degree of a proper dominant map \(f : X \rightarrow Y\) of equi-dimensional varieties \(X, Y\) along the pull back \( f ^{-1} (W)\) of a closed irreducible subvariety \(W \subset Y. \) If \(Z_i\), \(1 \leq i \leq k\) are the ireducibel components of \(f ^{-1} (W) = \sum _{i=1} ^k Z_i\) then \(\deg (f) = \sum _{i=1} ^k \deg ( f \vert _{Z_i}). \) The morphism \( f : X \rightarrow Y\) is associated with a map \(\widetilde{f} : \mathrm{Bl} _{Z_i} X \rightarrow\mathrm{Bl} _W Y\) of the corresponding blow ups, which restricts to a map \(f_* : \widetilde{Z_i} \rightarrow \widetilde{W}\) of the exceptional divisors. If \(f_*\) induces an injective morphism of \(\mathcal{N} _{Z \setminus X}\) in \(\mathcal{N} _{W \setminus Y}\) then \(\deg ( f \vert _{Z_i}) = \deg ( f_* \vert _{\widetilde{Z_i}}). \) The locus \(\mathcal{J} _5 \subset \mathcal{A}_5\) of the Jacobians of the smooth curves of genus \(5\) is of dimension \(12\) in the \(15\)-dimensional \( \mathcal{A}_5. \) Results of Mumford from 1974 and of Donagi-Smith from 1981 describe the allowable coverings \( \pi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\), whose Prym varieties equal the Jacobian of a generic smooth curve of genus \(5. \) These are parameterized by two irreducible subvarieties of \( \mathcal{R}_6\) and two boundary components of \( \overline{\mathcal{R}_6}. \)

The sixth section studies the locus \(\mathcal{R}' _{\mathcal{Q}}\) of \([C, \eta] \in \mathcal{R}_6\) with a smooth plane quintic \(C \subset {\mathbb P}^2 ( {\mathbb C})\) and some \( \eta \in\mathrm{Pic} ^0(C) \setminus \{ \mathcal{O}_C \}\) with \(\eta ^{\otimes 2} = \mathcal{O}_C. \) The hyperplane class of \({\mathbb P}^2 ( {\mathbb C})\) induces a line bundle \( \kappa \rightarrow C\) with \( \kappa ^{\otimes 2} = \Omega _C\) and odd \(\dim H ^0 (C, \kappa). \) As a result, there is a decomposition \(\mathcal{R}' _{\mathcal{Q}} = \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{Q}} \cup \mathcal{R} _{\mathcal{C}}\) into a disjoint union of \(\mathcal{R} _{\mathcal{Q}} \ni [C, \eta]\) with even \(\dim H^0 (C, \eta \otimes \kappa)\) and \(\mathcal{R} _{\mathcal{C}} \ni [C, \eta]\) with odd \(\dim H^0 (C, \eta \otimes \kappa)\). The sixth section explains why \( \mathcal{P}_6 : \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{Q}} \rightarrow \mathcal{J} _5\) is surjective and of local degree \(1. \) The action of the Prym map on the odd coverings \(\mathcal{R} _{\mathcal{C}}\) of the plane quintic \(C\) is deferred to section nine.

The seventh section discusses Recillas' bijective correspondence between the tetragonal curves \(X\) of genus \(g-1\) and the étale double covering \(\pi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\) of trigonal curves \(C\) of genus \(g, \) whose Prym varieties \(P ( \pi ) = JX\) equal the Jacobian of \(X. \) The Abel-Prym map \( \psi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow P ( \pi)\) of \( \pi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\) is expressed by the Abel-Jacobi map \( \alpha : X \rightarrow JX\). This section explains why the local degree of \( \overline{\mathcal{P}_6}\) on the compactification \( \overline{\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal T}}\) of the moduli space \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal T}\) of the double coverings of the trigonal curves of genus \(6\), is of local degree \(10. \)

The eight section is devoted to the action of \( \overline{\mathcal{P}_6} : \overline{\mathcal{R} _6} \rightarrow {\mathcal J}_5\) on the boundary \( \partial \mathcal{R}_6 = \overline{\mathcal{R}_6} \setminus \mathcal{R}_6\). The Wirtinger coverings \( \pi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\) include the ones with an irreducible \(C, \) having a single node, and their degenerations. If \(X\) is a smooth curve of genus \(5, \) \(X_1 \simeq X_2\) are copies of \(X, \) \( \widetilde{E}\) is and étale double cover of an elliptic curve \(E\), then the double coverings \(\pi : \left(\widetilde{C} = X_1 \cup \widetilde{E} \cup X_2 / p_1 \sim 0, p_2 \sim a \right) \rightarrow \left( C = X \cup E / p \sim 0 \right)\) for some \(p_i \in X_i\) with \( \pi (p_i) = p \in X\) and some \(0, a \in \widetilde{E} \) with \( \pi (0) = \pi (a) = 0 \in E, \) are called elliptic tales. The moduli spaces \( \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{S}}\) of the Wirtinger coverings and \( \mathcal{R}_E\) of the elliptic tails are irreducible components of \(\partial \mathcal{R}_6, \) whose images under \( \overline{\mathcal{P}_6}\) contain \({\mathcal J}_5. \) The only other irreducible component of \(\partial \mathcal{R}_6, \) whose image contains \({\mathcal J}_5, \) is the boundary \( \partial \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal T} = \overline{\mathcal{R} _{\mathcal{T}}} \setminus \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{T}}\) of the allowable coverings of the trigonal curves. After blowing up \( \mathcal{M}_5\) in \( \mathcal{A}_5 \) and restricting to the exceptional divisors, the local degree of \( \overline{\mathcal{P}_6} \vert _{\partial \mathcal{R}_6}\) is computed to be \(16. \)

The ninth section discuses the fibres of \( \mathcal{P}_6 \vert _{\mathcal{R} _{\mathcal{C}}}\) after describing the image \( \mathcal{P}_6 ( \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal {C}}) \subset \mathcal{M}_5\) as the locus of the intermediate Jacobians of the cubic hypersurfaces \( X \subset {\mathbb P}^4 ( {\mathbb C}). \) Let us recall that a generic hyperplane in \({\mathbb P}^4 ( {\mathbb C})\) intersects \(X\) in \(27\) lines, which form a \(2\)-dimensional family, parameterized by a Fano surface \(F(X). \) As a principally polarized abelian variety, the intermediate Jacobian \(JX = H ^{1,2} (X, {\mathbb C}) / H^3 (X, {\mathbb Z})\) of \(X\) is isomorphic to the Albanese variety \(\mathrm{Alb} (F(X))\) of \(F(X). \) The correspondence, associating to a cubic threefold \(X \subset {\mathbb P}^4 ( {\mathbb C})\) its intermediate Jacobian \(JX\) induces a map \( \mathcal{C} \rightarrow \mathcal{A}_5\) of the \(10\)-dimensional moduli space \( \mathcal{C}\) of the cubic threfolds \(X\). Let \(l_0\) be a generic line in \({\mathbb P}^4 ( {\mathbb C}), \) which is contained in \(X, \) \(\mathrm{Bl} : \mathrm{Bl} _{l_0} X \rightarrow X\) be the blow up of \(X\) along \(l_0\) and \( \pi _{l_o} : X \rightarrow {\mathbb P}^2 ( {\mathbb C})\) be the projection from \(l_0\) to \({\mathbb P}^2 ( {\mathbb C}). \) Then \(\mathrm{pr} = \pi _{l_0}\mathrm{Bl} : \widetilde{X} \rightarrow {\mathbb P}^2 ( {\mathbb C})\) is a conic bundle and the set \(C\) of the points \(p \in {\mathbb P}^2 ( {\mathbb C})\), over which the fibre \(\mathrm{pr} ^{-1} (p)\) contains two lines is a smooth plane quintic. The set \(\widetilde{C}\) of the lines \(l \in F(X)\), intersecting \(l_0\) is a smooth curve, on which the restriction \(\pi =\mathrm{pr} \vert _{\widetilde{C}} : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\) is an étale double covering. The ninth section explains that the Prym variety \(P ( \pi ) \simeq JX\) of \( \pi \) is the intermediate Jacobian of \(X\) and the fibre \( \mathcal{P} _g ^{-1} (JX)\) of the Prym map over \(P ( \pi) = JX\) is isomorphic to \(F(X). \) The \(2\)-torsion point \(\eta \in JC, \) associated with \(\pi : \widetilde{C} \rightarrow C\) corresponds to an odd covering \([C, \eta] \in \mathcal{R} _{\mathcal{C}}\) and the entire fibre \( \mathcal{P}_6 ^{-1} (JX)\) is contained in \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{C}}. \) Moreover, \( \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal C}\) is the closure of the union of the subvarieties of \({\mathcal P}_6 ^{-1} (JX)\), parameterized by \(F(X), \) for all smooth cubic threefolds \(X\) and the local degree of the Prym map over \( \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{C}}\) is \(27. \)

The tenth section explains how the tetragonal correspondence on a fibre \( \mathcal{P}_6 ^{-1} (A)\) over a generic point \(A \in \mathcal{A}_5\) is equivalent to the incidence correspondence of the \(27\) lines on a smooth cubic surface. The Galois group of the Galois closure of \(\mathcal{R}_6 \rightarrow \mathcal{A}_5\) is identified with the Weyl group \(W(E_6)\) of the symmetries of the incidence of these \(27\) lines.

The last, eleventh section contains several solved exercises, which can be viewed as non-trivial applications of the described machinery from the theory of complex curves and the theory of abelian varieties.

title.title: Prym varieties and Prym map

editorial_contributions.text:
This paper decomposes up to isogeny the intermediate Jacobians of a special type of cubic threefolds. Let \(X\) be a smooth cubic threefold defined over \(\mathbb{C}\) admitting an automorphism of order five. Such cubic threefolds are described in [\textit{V. González-Aguilera} and \textit{A. Liendo}, Arch. Math. 97, No. 1, 25--37 (2011; Zbl 1231.14033)] using explicit equations. The main result of this paper is that the intermediate Jacobian \(J(X)\) of \(X\) is isogenous to \(E\times B^2\), where \(E\) is an elliptic curve and \(B\) is an abelian surface with real multiplication by \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})\), i.e. \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})\subset\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb{C}}(B)\otimes_{\mathbb Z} \mathbb{Q}\). Furthermore, the authors shows that the same conclusion also holds for \(X\) defined over any field \(k\) of characteristic zero containing a primitive fifth root of unity.

Following \textit{J. P. Murre} [Compos. Math. 25, 161--206 (1972; Zbl 0242.14002)], the authors construct explicitly from \(X\) an algebraic curve \(\mathcal H_l\) with an involution \(\iota_l\), so that the Prym variety associated to the double cover \(\mathcal H_l\to\mathcal H_l/\iota_l\) is the intermediate Jacobian \(J(X)\). Under this geometric interpretation of \(J(X)\), the authors are able to construct concrete models of its elliptic component \(E\) and its abelian surface component \(B\) up to isogeny.

The proofs and the constructions in this paper are explicit and hence very accessible to readers.

citingPaper.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth cubic threefold. By invoking ideas from Geometric Manin's Conjecture, we give a complete description of the main components of the Kontsevich moduli space of genus one stable maps $\overline{M}_{1,0}(X)$. In particular, we show that for degree $e\geqslant 5$, there are exactly two irreducible main components, of which one generically parametrizes free curves birational onto their images, and the other corresponds to degree $e$ covers of lines. As a corollary, we classify components of the morphism space $\text{Mor}(E,X)$ for a general smooth genus one curve $E$.

citingPaper.abstract:
Abstract For any power q of the positive ground field characteristic, a smooth q-bic threefold—the Fermat threefold of degree 
$q+1$
 , for example—has a smooth surface S of lines which behaves like the Fano surface of a smooth cubic threefold. I develop projective, moduli-theoretic, and degeneration techniques to study the geometry of S. Using, in addition, the modular representation theory of the finite unitary group and the geometric theory of filtrations, I compute the cohomology of the structure sheaf of S when q is prime.

citingPaper.abstract: For $X$ a smooth cubic threefold we study the Pl\"ucker embedding of the Fano surface of lines $S$ of $X$. We prove that if $X$ is general then the minimal gonality of a covering family of curves of $S$ is four and that this happens for a unique family of curves. The analysis also shows that there is a unique pentagonal connecting family of curves, which leads to the fact that the connecting gonality of $S$ is five whereas the degree of irrationality, i.e.\ the minimal degree of a rational map from $S$ to $\mathbb{P}^2$, is six.

citingPaper.abstract: We show that Albanese varieties of abelian covers of projective plane are isogenous to product of isogeny components of abelian varieties associated with singularities of the ramification locus. In particular Albanese varieties of abelian covers of P ramified over arrangements of lines and uniformized by unit ball in C are isogenous to a product of Jacobians of Fermat curves. Periodicity of the sequence of (semi-abelian) Albanese varieties of unramified cyclic covers of complements to a plane singular curve is shown.

citingPaper.abstract: Let $Y$ be a cubic threefold with a non-Eckardt type involution $\tau$. Our first main result is that the $\tau$-equivariant category of the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(Y)$ determines the isomorphism class of $Y$ for general $(Y,\tau)$. We shall prove this categorical Torelli theorem via three approaches: a noncommutative Hodge theoretical one (using a generalization of the intermediate Jacobian construction due to Alexander Perry), a Bridgeland moduli theoretical one (using equivariant stability conditions), and a Chow theoretical one (using some techniques in [kuznetsovnonclodedfield2021]).The remaining part of the paper is devoted to proving an equivariant infinitesimal categorical Torelli for non-Eckardt cubic threefolds $(Y,\tau)$. To accomplish it, we prove a compatibility theorem on the algebra structures of the Hochschild cohomology of the bounded derived category $D^b(X)$ of a smooth projective variety $X$ and on the Hochschild cohomology of a semi-orthogonal component of $D^b(X)$. Another key ingredient is a generalization of a result in [macri2009infinitesima] which shows that the twisted Hochschild-Kostant-Rosenberg isomorphism is compatible with the actions on the Hochschild cohomology and on the singular cohomology induced by an automorphism of $X$. In appendix, we prove an equivariant categorical Torelli theorem for arbitrary cubic threefold with a geometric involution under a natural assumption.
